In the transportation business, amid continued labor shortages and soaring crude oil prices, the company is working to improve efficiency by sharing and utilizing logistics resources within the group. In the car rental business, while the industry as a whole is growing on inbound demand, new entrants have increased and price competition has intensified, and the company is securing profit by raising utilization rates and improving unit prices. entries.9d8d31532d2ed95d: This business sells housing construction materials, housing equipment, lumber and similar products, and engages in construction work and real estate sales, purchases and leasing. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥99,296 million (up 0.6% year on year), accounting for 9.2% of consolidated revenue. Results of subsidiaries including Fudosan no Osawa Co., Ltd., which joined the group in the previous fiscal year, were included for the full year. On the other hand, rising housing prices and higher mortgage rates reduced the purchase intentions of prospective homebuyers, and, owing to the 'rush of construction starts' ahead of the full enforcement in April 2025 of the revised Act on the Improvement of Energy Consumption Performance of Buildings and the revised Building Standards Act, the number of new housing starts has continued to decline since April of that year. The company is strengthening efforts to propose lumber and building materials together for properties for which it has received pre-cut orders. The principal affiliated companies listed are 11 companies, including Yamae Kuno Co., Ltd., Waitec Co., Ltd., Hibic Co., Ltd., Yamae Realty Co., Ltd., Astique Co., Ltd., Yamae BUILD Co., Ltd. and Kokoro Kensetsu Co., Ltd.

entries.c95490e76042dda4: This business centers on the sale of processed general foods, confectionery, alcoholic beverages and frozen foods, and also includes manufacture of boxed lunches and shochu, manufacture, processing and sale of agricultural and marine products, and delivery food services. It is the largest business in the group; revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥839,047 million (up 9.2% year on year), accounting for 77.3% of consolidated revenue. Demand was firm mainly in the food service industry, and revenue increased as the company worked on sales promotion that captured changes in market structure and purchasing behavior, expanded high value-added products, and improved logistics and manufacturing efficiency. On the other hand, as food and beverage prices continued to rise, consumers became more inclined to save, and sales competition with peer companies has intensified. The principal affiliated companies listed number 15, including Yamae Kuno Co., Ltd., Minori Holdings Co., Ltd., Kawachiya Genos Co., Ltd., Confex Holdings Co., Ltd. and Nippon Pizza Hut Co., Ltd.
